g.title: BrainMaster
g.text: ONE brain (one network, one update loop): a NAVIGATION half and a CONVERSATION half as separate groups of neurons on the same substrate
they interact through THREE validated synaptic routes — A: a spoken word steers the body · B: navigate to SEE an object then RECALL it · C: bind a PERCEIVED object into a new fact
navigation decides which way to move by a spiking race (no hand-coded shortcut) · conversation answers "I don't know" rather than inventing (the no-confabulation safeguard)
honest map of the code, including its simplifications (faithful-vs-shortcut layer)

g.title: cluster_shared
g.text: · built (as the same type) by BOTH configs

g.title: cluster_conv
g.text: · the production pipeline (OneBrainComposer) · the language brain

g.title: cluster_gen
g.text: · recognise a NOVEL object by its category, then answer about it · co-resident opt-in

g.title: nav_in
g.text: ⌂ sensory input the world renders for the agent

g.title: bg
g.text: the decision heart · where it learns

g.title: sc
g.text: evidence builds up → an all-or-none "commit" burst picks the move (×4)
DEFAULT: the move emerges from the spiking race
the hand-coded argmax is RETIRED · 6/6-seed GO · 100% commit-burst

g.title: motor
g.text: the body moves the way the firing pool says

g.title: cortex320
g.text: similar words sit close together (so it can generalize)

g.title: visual->lang_out
g.text: B · see an object, later RECALL it
vision → words route + memory tag · navigate-to-see · 6/6-seed GO

g.title: composer
g.text: Composer — bind words into a fact
handles attributes ("big apple"), negation, embedded clauses · ~10–20× faster
⚠ binding rule is fixed algebra (stand-in for a learned cortex — step 3)

g.title: visual->composer
g.text: C · bind a PERCEIVED object into a new fact
a seen object's firing → a code the composer can bind · navigate-to-compose · 6/6-seed GO

g.title: lang_in->m1
g.text: A · a spoken word steers the body
learned word→action route · opened by comprehension · 6/6-seed GO

g.title: parser
g.text: voice-invariant · flexible frames (S-V-O / V-S-O / O-S-V, auto-picked)

g.title: store
g.text: each fact = a pattern written into complex synapses

g.title: recall
g.text: who/what · yes-no · multi-hop reasoning · multi-turn dialogue
answers "I don't know" rather than inventing

g.title: dlg
g.text: picks the next on-topic thing to say

g.title: produce
g.text: a spiking "say-this-first" ranking orders the words
competitive-queuing serial order (not a host template)

g.title: gen_conc
g.text: slow integration lets a faint percept reach firing

g.title: gen_fact
g.text: → recall a fact about that category

g.title: leg
g.text: How to read this map — box colour = which half builds it
slow inhibition (GABA-B) — the one signature "value subtraction" edge
dopamine — a reinforcement signal sprayed widely (not a wire)
━━▶ the two halves interact through these routes (each 6/6-seed GO):
a spoken word steers the moving body
navigate to SEE an object, then RECALL what was seen
bind a PERCEIVED object into a new fact
(full detail: the two detail diagrams + the spec)
input/output boundary — the world renders what the agent senses, the body acts on its output (LEGITIMATE, not a shortcut)
a documented SHORTCUT — a simplified stand-in, or a step still done by host maths instead of neurons
a switchable gate that opens/closes a route at run time
= the conversation answers "I don't know" instead of guessing
simplifications everywhere: point neurons (no dendrites) · one-step delays · simplified
neuron + synapse models (the full list SH-1…SH-14 is in the spec)
= nav + conversation on one network, one update loop. The conversation half is held
frozen during navigation so its memory can't drift; the A/B/C routes + generalization are opt-in add-ons.
